EN

Understanding Spec-Driven Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl

中文

理解规格驱动开发：Kiro、spec-kit 与 Tessl

EN

Birgitta Böckeler
Distinguished Engineer and AI-assisted delivery expert at Thoughtworks, with more than 20 years of experience as a software developer, architect, and technical leader.

中文

Birgitta Böckeler
Thoughtworks 杰出工程师、AI 辅助交付专家，拥有 20 多年软件开发、架构与技术领导经验。

EN

This article is part of “Exploring Gen AI”, a series capturing Thoughtworks technologists’ explorations of using generative AI for software development.

15 October 2025

中文

本文属于“探索生成式 AI（Exploring Gen AI）”系列，记录 Thoughtworks 技术人员对生成式 AI 在软件开发中应用方式的探索。

2025 年 10 月 15 日

EN

I’ve been trying to understand one of the latest AI coding buzzwords: Spec-driven development (SDD). I looked at three tools that describe themselves as SDD tools and tried to untangle what the term means today.

中文

最近我一直在尝试理解 AI 编程领域的一个新热词：规格驱动开发（Spec-Driven Development，SDD）。我考察了三款自称采用 SDD 的工具，并试图厘清这个概念在当下究竟意味着什么。

Definition定义

EN

Like many emerging terms in this fast-moving field, the definition of “spec-driven development” is still changing. From the ways I have seen it used so far, I would summarize it like this: SDD means writing a “spec” before writing code with AI — a documentation-first approach. The spec becomes the source of truth for both the human and the AI.

中文

与这个快速演进领域中的许多新兴术语一样，“规格驱动开发”的定义仍在变化。根据我目前看到的用法，可以将它概括为：在使用 AI 编写代码之前，先编写一份“规格说明（spec）”，也就是一种“文档优先”的方式。规格说明会成为人和 AI 共同遵循的事实来源。

EN

GitHub: “In this new world, maintaining software means evolving specifications. […] The lingua franca of development moves to a higher level, and code is the last-mile approach.”

中文

GitHub：“在这个新世界里，维护软件意味着持续演进规格说明。……开发的通用语言上升到了更高层级，而代码则成为最后一公里的实现手段。”

EN

Tessl: “A development approach where specs — not code — are the primary artifact. Specs describe intent in structured, testable language, and agents generate code to match them.”

中文

Tessl：“一种以规格说明而非代码作为主要产物的开发方式。规格说明使用结构化、可测试的语言表达意图，而智能体生成与之匹配的代码。”

EN

After reviewing how the term is used, and the tools that claim to implement it, it seems that SDD actually has several implementation levels:

  1. Spec-first: A well-considered spec is written first and then used in the AI-assisted development workflow for the task at hand.
  2. Spec-anchored: The spec is retained after the task is complete and continues to guide the evolution and maintenance of the feature.
  3. Spec-as-source: The spec remains the primary source file over time. Humans edit only the spec and never edit the generated code directly.
中文

在梳理了这个术语的各种用法以及声称实现 SDD 的工具之后，我感觉现实中的 SDD 至少存在多个实现层级：

  1. 规格优先（Spec-first）：先认真编写规格说明，再将其用于当前任务的 AI 辅助开发流程。
  2. 规格锚定（Spec-anchored）：任务完成后仍保留规格说明，并继续用它指导相应功能的演进与维护。
  3. 规格即源码（Spec-as-source）：长期以规格说明作为主要源文件；人只编辑规格说明，从不直接修改生成的代码。
EN

Every SDD approach and definition I found is spec-first, but not all of them aim to be spec-anchored or spec-as-source. The long-term maintenance strategy for the spec is often vague or left completely open.

中文

我找到的所有 SDD 方法和定义都属于“规格优先”，但并非都追求“规格锚定”或“规格即源码”。对于规格说明长期应如何维护，很多方案都语焉不详，甚至完全没有规定。

What is a spec?什么是规格说明？

EN

The key definitional question is, of course: What is a spec? There does not appear to be a general definition. The closest thing to a consistent description is a comparison with a Product Requirements Document.

中文

定义上的核心问题当然是：什么才算规格说明？目前似乎不存在统一定义。最接近一致说法的，是把它类比为“产品需求文档（Product Requirements Document）”。

EN

The term is heavily overloaded at the moment. Here is my attempt at a definition:

A spec is a structured, behavior-oriented artifact — or a set of related artifacts — written in natural language, expressing software functionality and serving as guidance for AI coding agents. Each SDD variant defines its own structure, level of detail, and organization of these artifacts inside a project.

中文

目前这个词承载了太多不同含义。下面是我尝试给出的定义：

规格说明是一种以自然语言编写、结构化且面向行为的产物，也可以是一组相互关联的产物；它用于表达软件功能，并为 AI 编程智能体提供指导。每一种 SDD 变体都会自行定义规格说明的结构、详细程度，以及这些产物在项目中的组织方式。

EN

It is useful to distinguish specs from the more general context documents for a codebase. General context includes rules files and high-level descriptions of the product or codebase. Some tools call this a memory bank, so I will use that term here. These files matter across all AI coding sessions in the repository, while a spec is relevant only to tasks that create or change a particular piece of functionality.

中文

我认为有必要区分“规格说明”和代码库中更通用的上下文文档。通用上下文包括规则文件，以及对产品或代码库的高层描述。一些工具把这类内容称为“记忆库（memory bank）”，本文也沿用这一说法。这些文件会影响代码库中的所有 AI 编程会话，而规格说明通常只与创建或修改某项特定功能的任务相关。

The challenge with evaluating SDD tools评估 SDD 工具的难点

EN

Evaluating SDD tools and approaches in a way that resembles real use turns out to be time-consuming. You would need to try them on problems of different sizes, in both greenfield and brownfield codebases, and spend real time reviewing and revising intermediate artifacts rather than merely glancing at them. As GitHub’s post about spec-kit puts it: “Crucially, your role isn’t just to steer. It’s to verify. At each phase, you reflect and refine.”

中文

事实证明，要以接近真实使用的方式评估 SDD 工具和方法，需要投入相当多的时间。你必须在不同规模的问题上尝试它们，覆盖全新项目和既有代码库，并认真审查、修改中间产物，而不是草草扫一眼。正如 GitHub 关于 spec-kit 的文章所说：“关键在于，你的角色不只是引导，还要验证。在每个阶段，你都要反思并改进。”

EN

For two of the three tools I tried, introducing them into an existing codebase also appeared to require even more work, making their usefulness for brownfield systems especially difficult to assess. Until I hear reports from people who have used them for a sustained period on a real codebase, I will still have many open questions about how this works in practice.

中文

在我尝试的三款工具中，有两款要引入既有代码库似乎还需要额外的大量工作，因此更难判断它们对棕地系统到底有多大价值。在听到有人长期将它们用于真实代码库的实践报告之前，我对它们在现实中的运作方式仍会保留许多疑问。

EN

With that said, let’s look at the three tools. I will first describe how they work — or rather, how I believe they work — and leave my observations and questions until the end. These tools are evolving very quickly, so they may already have changed since I used them in September.

中文

话虽如此，下面还是来看看这三款工具。我会先描述它们如何工作——更准确地说，是我认为它们如何工作——并把观察和问题留到最后。需要注意的是，这些工具演进非常快，自我在九月份试用之后，它们可能已经发生变化。

KiroKiro

EN

Kiro is the simplest, or most lightweight, of the three tools I tried. It appears to be primarily spec-first. Every example I found uses it for a task or user story, without explaining how the requirements document should be maintained over time in a spec-anchored way across multiple tasks.

中文

Kiro 是我尝试的三款工具中最简单、也最轻量的一款。它看起来主要属于“规格优先”。我找到的示例都把它用于一个任务或一条用户故事，却没有说明如何跨多个任务长期维护需求文档，从而形成“规格锚定”的实践。

EN

Workflow: Requirements → Design → Tasks

中文

工作流：需求 → 设计 → 任务

EN

Each workflow step is represented by one Markdown document, and Kiro guides you through those three steps inside its VS Code-based distribution.

中文

工作流中的每一步都对应一份 Markdown 文档，Kiro 会在其基于 VS Code 的发行版本中引导你依次完成这三个步骤。

EN

Requirements: A list of requirements. Each requirement represents a user story in “As a…” form, with acceptance criteria written in “GIVEN… WHEN… THEN…” form.

中文

需求：以需求列表的形式组织。每条需求代表一条采用“As a…”格式的用户故事，并附带使用“GIVEN… WHEN… THEN…”格式编写的验收标准。

EN

Design: In my experiment, the design document contained the sections visible in the screenshot below. I retained the result from only one attempt, so I do not know whether this structure is consistent or varies with the task.

中文

设计：在我的一次尝试中，设计文档包含了下图所示的章节。我只保留了一次尝试的结果，因此无法确认这种结构是否固定，还是会根据任务变化。

EN

Tasks: A list of tasks that trace back to requirement numbers, with additional UI controls for running tasks one by one and reviewing the changes for each task.

中文

任务：任务列表中的每项任务都可以追溯到对应的需求编号，并带有额外的界面控件，可逐项执行任务并审查每项任务产生的改动。

EN

Kiro also has a memory-bank concept that it calls steering. Its contents are flexible, and the workflow does not appear to depend on any particular files being present — I made my trial runs before I even discovered the steering area. When you ask Kiro to generate steering documents, the default structure is product.md, structure.md, and tech.md.

中文

Kiro 也有“记忆库”概念，称为 steering（引导）。其中的内容较为灵活，工作流似乎也不依赖某些固定文件是否存在——事实上，我完成试用之后才发现这个区域。当你让 Kiro 生成 steering 文档时，默认结构包含 product.md、structure.md 和 tech.md。

Spec-kitSpec-kit

EN

Spec-kit is GitHub’s implementation of SDD. It is distributed as a CLI that can create workspace setups for many common coding assistants. Once the structure is in place, you interact with spec-kit through slash commands in your coding assistant. Because all artifacts live directly in the workspace, this is the most customizable of the three tools discussed here.

中文

Spec-kit 是 GitHub 对 SDD 的实现。它以 CLI 形式发布，可为多种常见编程助手创建工作区结构。结构建立后，你通过编程助手中的斜杠命令与 spec-kit 交互。由于所有产物都直接放在工作区中，它是本文三款工具里可定制性最高的一款。

EN

Workflow: Constitution → 𝄆 Specify → Plan → Tasks 𝄇

中文

工作流：宪章 → 𝄆 规格化 → 计划 → 任务 𝄇

EN

Spec-kit’s memory-bank concept is a prerequisite for its spec-driven approach. It calls this the constitution. The constitution is intended to hold high-level principles that are “immutable” and should apply to every change. In effect, it is a very powerful rules file that the workflow uses heavily.

中文

在 spec-kit 中，记忆库是其规格驱动方法的前置条件。它把这份内容称为“宪章（constitution）”。宪章应包含“不可变”的高层原则，并应用于每一次变更。实质上，它是一份能力很强、且在工作流中被大量使用的规则文件。

EN

At each workflow step — specify, plan, and tasks — spec-kit uses shell scripts and templates to instantiate a set of files and prompts. The workflow then relies heavily on checklists inside those files to track required user clarifications, constitution violations, research tasks, and more. These lists act like a definition of done for each step, although they are interpreted by AI, so there is no absolute guarantee that they will be followed.

中文

在工作流的每个阶段——规格化、计划和任务——spec-kit 都会借助 shell 脚本与模板实例化一组文件和提示词。随后，工作流会大量依赖文件中的检查清单，以跟踪必须向用户澄清的问题、对宪章的违反、研究任务等。这些清单类似每个阶段的“完成定义”，但由于最终由 AI 解读，因此无法百分之百保证它们会被遵守。

EN

The diagram below illustrates the file topology I saw in spec-kit. Notice that a single spec is composed of many files.

中文

下图展示了我在 spec-kit 中观察到的文件拓扑。请注意，一份规格说明实际上由许多文件共同构成。

EN

At first glance, GitHub seems to aspire to a spec-anchored approach: specifications are treated not as static documents, but as living, executable artifacts that evolve with the project and serve as a shared source of truth. When something does not make sense, you return to the spec; as complexity grows, you refine it; when tasks are too large, you break them down.

中文

乍看之下，GitHub 似乎希望采用“规格锚定”的方式：规格说明不是静态文档，而是会随项目演进、可执行的活产物，并作为共享的事实来源。遇到不合理之处时回到规格说明；项目变复杂时继续细化；任务过大时再拆分。

EN

However, spec-kit creates a branch for every new spec. That suggests it treats a spec as a living artifact for the lifetime of a change request, rather than for the lifetime of a feature. A community discussion reflects this confusion. This makes me think that spec-kit is still what I would call spec-first only, rather than spec-anchored over time.

中文

然而，spec-kit 会为每份新规格说明创建一个分支。这似乎表明，它把规格说明视为在一次变更请求生命周期内存续的产物，而不是在某项功能的整个生命周期中存续。社区讨论中也有人提出了这种困惑。因此我倾向于认为，spec-kit 目前仍只是我所说的“规格优先”，还没有真正实现长期的“规格锚定”。

Tessl FrameworkTessl Framework

EN

(Still in private beta)

中文

（仍处于私有 Beta 阶段）

EN

Like spec-kit, the Tessl Framework is distributed as a CLI that can create workspace and configuration structures for a variety of coding assistants. The same CLI command can also operate as an MCP server.

中文

与 spec-kit 类似，Tessl Framework 也以 CLI 形式发布，可以为多种编程助手创建工作区和配置结构。同一个 CLI 命令还可以作为 MCP 服务器运行。

EN

Tessl is the only one of these three tools that explicitly aims for a spec-anchored approach, and it is even exploring the spec-as-source level of SDD. A Tessl spec can be the main artifact that is maintained and edited, while the code is marked at the top with // GENERATED FROM SPEC - DO NOT EDIT. At present, the mapping is one-to-one: one spec generates one file in the codebase.

中文

Tessl 是这三款工具中唯一明确以“规格锚定”为目标的工具，甚至还在探索 SDD 的“规格即源码”层级。Tessl 规格说明可以成为被持续维护和编辑的主要产物，而代码文件顶部会标记 // GENERATED FROM SPEC - DO NOT EDIT。目前两者是一对一映射：一份规格说明对应代码库中的一个文件。

EN

Tessl is still in beta and the team is experimenting with different forms of this model. I can imagine the mapping moving to a higher level, where one spec corresponds to a component consisting of multiple files. What the alpha product will eventually support remains to be seen. The Tessl team itself views the framework as more future-facing than its current public product, Tessl Registry.

中文

不过 Tessl 仍处于 Beta 阶段，团队也在尝试这种模型的不同版本。我可以想象，未来映射关系可能提升到更高层级：一份规格说明对应由多个文件组成的一个代码组件。最终 Alpha 产品会支持什么，还有待观察。Tessl 团队自己也认为，这套 Framework 更像是面向未来的方向，而非当前公开产品 Tessl Registry 的现状。

EN

Here is an example of a spec that I asked the Tessl CLI to reverse-engineer from a JavaScript file in an existing codebase using tessl document --code ...js:

中文

下面是一份示例规格说明：我让 Tessl CLI 使用 tessl document --code ...js，从既有代码库中的一个 JavaScript 文件反向生成了它。

EN

Tags such as @generate and @test appear to tell Tessl what to generate. The API section illustrates the idea of defining, in the spec, at least the interfaces exposed to the rest of the codebase — presumably so that these critical parts of the generated component remain fully controlled by the maintainer. Running tessl build then generates the corresponding JavaScript file.

中文

@generate、@test 等标签似乎用于告诉 Tessl 应生成哪些内容。API 章节体现了一种思路：至少要在规格说明中定义暴露给代码库其他部分的接口，以确保生成组件中这些关键部分仍完全受维护者控制。执行 tessl build 后，Tessl 会生成对应的 JavaScript 文件。

EN

Keeping spec-as-source specifications at a relatively low abstraction level, one per code file, probably reduces the number of steps and interpretations required from the LLM, and therefore reduces the chance of error. Even at this low level, however, I observed non-determinism when generating code multiple times from the same spec. It was instructive to refine the spec repeatedly, making it more precise to improve repeatability.

中文

如果把“规格即源码”的规格说明放在较低抽象层级——每个代码文件对应一份规格说明——可能会减少大语言模型需要完成的步骤和解释次数，从而降低出错概率。不过，即使在这么低的抽象层级，我仍然观察到了非确定性：从同一份规格说明多次生成代码，结果并不完全相同。不断迭代规格说明、让它越来越具体，以提升代码生成的可重复性，是一个很有意思的练习。

EN

That process reminded me of the familiar pitfalls and challenges involved in writing an unambiguous and complete specification.

中文

这个过程也让我重新想起：要写出没有歧义、足够完整的规格说明，本身就存在许多熟悉的陷阱和挑战。

Observations and questions观察与疑问

EN

All three tools label themselves as implementations of spec-driven development, yet they differ substantially. That is the first thing to keep in mind when discussing SDD: it is not a single, uniform thing.

中文

这三款工具都把自己称为规格驱动开发的实现，但彼此差异很大。因此，在讨论 SDD 时首先要记住：它并不是一种单一、统一的方法。

One workflow to fit all sizes?一种工作流能适配所有规模吗？

EN

Kiro and spec-kit each provide one opinionated workflow, but I am fairly sure neither workflow is suitable for most real-world coding problems. In particular, it is unclear how either one can accommodate a wide enough range of problem sizes to be generally applicable.

中文

Kiro 和 spec-kit 各自提供了一套带有强烈主张的工作流，但我相当确信，这两套流程都不适合大多数真实世界中的编程问题。尤其不清楚的是，它们如何覆盖足够广泛的问题规模，从而具备普遍适用性。

EN

When I asked Kiro to fix a small bug — the same bug I had previously used to test Codex — it quickly became obvious that the workflow was like using a sledgehammer to crack a nut. The requirements document expanded the tiny bug into four user stories and sixteen acceptance criteria, including statements such as: “As a developer, I want the transformation function to handle edge cases gracefully, so that the system remains robust when new category formats are introduced.”

中文

当我让 Kiro 修复一个很小的缺陷——也是我之前测试 Codex 时使用的同一个问题——很快就能看出，这套工作流像是在用大锤砸坚果。需求文档把这个小缺陷扩张成了 4 条用户故事和总计 16 条验收标准，其中甚至包括这样的内容：“作为开发者，我希望转换函数能够妥善处理边界情况，从而在引入新的分类格式时保持系统稳健。”

EN

I encountered a similar issue with spec-kit: I was unsure what size of problem to give it. Tutorials generally build an application from scratch because that is easiest to demonstrate. One use case I tried was roughly equivalent to a three-to-five-point story on one of my former teams. It depended heavily on existing code and involved building an overview modal that summarized data from an existing dashboard.

中文

我使用 spec-kit 时遇到了类似问题：我不确定应该把多大的问题交给它。现有教程通常从零创建一个应用，因为这最容易演示。我最终尝试的一个用例，大致相当于我过去团队中的一条 3～5 点用户故事。它高度依赖既有代码，需要构建一个概览弹窗，汇总已有仪表盘中的多项数据。

EN

Given the number of steps spec-kit required and the quantity of Markdown files it produced for review, the process again felt excessive for the size of the problem. The task was larger than the one I gave Kiro, but the workflow was also far more elaborate. I never completed the implementation, and I suspect that in the time I spent running and reviewing spec-kit’s output, I could have implemented the feature with ordinary AI-assisted coding while feeling much more in control.

中文

考虑到 spec-kit 所需的步骤数量，以及它生成的大量待审查 Markdown 文件，这套流程对于该问题的规模仍显得过度。虽然任务比我交给 Kiro 的那个更大，但工作流也复杂得多。我甚至没有完成全部实现；我认为，在运行并审查 spec-kit 输出所花费的同样时间里，我完全可以采用普通的 AI 辅助编程完成该功能，而且会感觉对过程更有掌控力。

EN

An effective SDD tool would, at minimum, need to support several core workflows for different sizes and types of change.

中文

一个真正有效的 SDD 工具，至少应该能够针对不同规模、不同类型的变更，灵活提供若干种核心工作流。

Reviewing Markdown instead of reviewing code?用审查 Markdown 取代审查代码？

EN

As noted above, spec-kit created a great many Markdown files for me to review. They repeated one another, repeated information already present in the code, and some even contained code themselves. Overall, they were verbose and tedious to inspect. Kiro was somewhat easier because it produced only three files, and the mental model of “requirements → design → tasks” was more intuitive.

中文

如前所述，spec-kit 生成了大量需要我审查的 Markdown 文件。它们彼此重复，也重复代码中已有的信息，有些文件甚至直接包含代码。总体而言，这些内容冗长而乏味。Kiro 稍微好一些，因为它只产生三个文件，而且“需求 → 设计 → 任务”的心智模型更容易理解。

EN

Even so, Kiro was also far too verbose for the small bug I asked it to fix.

中文

不过，对于我要求修复的那个小缺陷，Kiro 依然显得过于冗长。

EN

To be honest, I would rather review code than all of these Markdown files. An effective SDD tool would need to provide an excellent spec-review experience.

中文

坦率地说，比起审查这一大堆 Markdown 文件，我宁愿直接审查代码。一个有效的 SDD 工具必须提供非常出色的规格审查体验。

A false sense of control?一种虚假的掌控感？

EN

Despite all the files, templates, prompts, workflows, and checklists, I frequently observed agents failing to follow all instructions. Context windows are indeed larger now, and this is often cited as an enabler of SDD. But a larger context window does not mean the AI will correctly notice and apply everything inside it.

中文

即使拥有这么多文件、模板、提示词、工作流和检查清单，我仍经常看到智能体最终没有遵循所有指令。现在的上下文窗口确实更大，这也常被视为 SDD 得以实现的条件之一；但窗口变大，并不意味着 AI 就一定能正确识别并应用其中的所有内容。

EN

For example, spec-kit includes a research stage during planning. It did a good job researching the existing code when I asked it to add a feature on top of that code. Yet the agent ultimately ignored the fact that its notes described existing classes; it treated them as a new specification and generated the classes again, creating duplicates.

中文

例如，spec-kit 在计划阶段包含一个研究步骤。当我要求它基于既有代码添加功能时，它对现有代码进行了大量研究，这一点很好。但最终，智能体忽略了研究笔记是在描述已有类，反而把这些内容当作新的规格说明，再次生成了同样的类，造成重复。

EN

I did not only see instructions being ignored. I also saw the agent go far beyond what was needed because it followed an instruction too eagerly — for example, one of the articles in the constitution.

中文

我看到的不只是智能体忽略指令；它有时也会因为过度积极地遵循某条指令而做得远超所需，例如过分执行宪章中的某一条款。

EN

Experience has shown that small, iterative steps are our best way of retaining control over what we build. That makes me skeptical of large amounts of up-front specification design, especially when the specifications are excessively verbose. An effective SDD tool would need to support an iterative approach, yet small work packages almost seem at odds with the core idea of SDD.

中文

过去的经验表明，要保持对构建过程的掌控，最好的方式是采用小步、迭代式推进。因此，我对大量前置规格设计持怀疑态度，尤其当规格说明过分冗长时更是如此。有效的 SDD 工具必须支持迭代式方法，但“小工作包”似乎又与 SDD 的核心理念存在某种张力。

How can functional and technical specs be separated effectively?如何有效分离功能规格与技术规格？

EN

A common SDD idea is to deliberately separate the functional specification from the technical implementation. The underlying aspiration, I assume, is that AI could eventually fill in the solution and implementation details, allowing the same spec to target different technology stacks.

中文

SDD 中一个常见主张，是有意识地将功能规格与技术实现分离。我猜其底层愿景是：最终可以由 AI 补全解决方案与实现细节，使同一份规格说明能够适配不同技术栈。

EN

In practice, while using spec-kit I often became confused about when to remain at the functional level and when to introduce technical details. The tutorials and documentation were not fully consistent either; there appeared to be different interpretations of what “purely functional” really means.

中文

但在实际使用 spec-kit 时，我经常困惑：什么时候应该停留在功能层面，什么时候应该加入技术细节。教程和文档本身也并不完全一致，对“纯功能性”究竟意味着什么，似乎存在不同解释。

EN

Thinking back to the many user stories I have read throughout my career that failed to separate requirements from implementation, I do not believe our profession has a particularly good track record here.

中文

回想职业生涯中读过的无数用户故事，其中很多都没能把需求与实现妥善分开。我并不认为整个行业在这方面有多么出色的历史表现。

Who is the target user?目标用户是谁？

EN

Many demos and tutorials for SDD tools involve defining product and feature goals, and even use terms such as “user story”. Perhaps the intention is to use AI to enable cross-skilling, with developers taking a larger role in requirements analysis. Or perhaps developers are expected to pair with product specialists while going through the workflow. None of this is made explicit, however; the material simply assumes that a developer will perform all of this analysis.

中文

许多 SDD 工具的演示和教程都会涉及定义产品目标、功能目标，甚至直接使用“用户故事”等术语。也许其意图是借助 AI 促进跨职能能力，让开发者更深入参与需求分析；又或者开发者应在执行工作流时与产品人员结对协作。但这些都没有被明确说明，材料只是默认开发者会完成全部分析工作。

EN

If that is the case, I again have to ask: What size and type of problem is SDD intended for? Probably not large features whose requirements are still highly uncertain, because those surely require specialist product and requirements skills, as well as research, stakeholder involvement, and many other steps.

中文

如果真是这样，我就不得不再次追问：SDD 究竟适合什么规模、什么类型的问题？它大概不适合需求仍高度不明确的大型功能，因为这类工作显然需要专业的产品与需求能力，也需要研究、利益相关者参与以及其他许多步骤。

Spec-anchored and spec-as-source: are we learning from the past?规格锚定与规格即源码：我们是否在吸取过去的经验？

EN

Many people compare SDD with TDD or BDD. For spec-as-source in particular, however, another important comparison is MDD — model-driven development. Early in my career I worked on several projects that relied heavily on MDD, and trying the Tessl Framework repeatedly reminded me of that experience. In MDD, models were essentially the specs, although they were not written in natural language; they might be expressed in custom UML or a textual DSL.

中文

很多人会把 SDD 与 TDD 或 BDD 类比。但对于“规格即源码”而言，另一个重要参照是 MDD——模型驱动开发。在职业生涯早期，我参与过几个大量使用 MDD 的项目，而试用 Tessl Framework 的过程不断让我想起那段经历。在 MDD 中，模型本质上就是规格说明，只不过不是自然语言，而是用定制 UML 或文本 DSL 表达。

EN

We built custom code generators that transformed those specifications into code.

中文

当时我们会构建定制代码生成器，把这些规格说明转换成代码。

EN

Ultimately, MDD never became mainstream for business applications. It occupies an awkward abstraction level and creates too much overhead and too many constraints. LLMs remove some of that overhead and those constraints, creating renewed hope that we can finally focus on writing specs and simply generate code from them. With LLMs, we are no longer constrained by a predefined, parseable specification language, and we no longer need to build elaborate custom code generators.

中文

最终，MDD 从未在业务应用领域真正普及。它处在一个尴尬的抽象层级，并带来了过多开销和约束。大语言模型消除了一部分 MDD 的开销和限制，因此人们重新产生希望：我们或许终于可以专注于编写规格说明，然后直接从中生成代码。借助大语言模型，我们不再受预定义、可解析规格语言的限制，也不再需要构建复杂的定制代码生成器。

EN

The price, of course, is the non-determinism of LLMs. The parseable structure of older approaches also had benefits that we are now losing: tools could help spec authors produce valid, complete, and internally consistent specifications. I wonder whether spec-as-source, and even spec-anchored approaches, might end up combining the disadvantages of both MDD and LLMs — inflexibility and non-determinism.

中文

当然，代价是大语言模型的非确定性。过去方法中的可解析结构也有我们现在正在失去的优点：工具可以帮助规格作者写出合法、完整、内部一致的规格说明。我不禁怀疑，“规格即源码”，甚至“规格锚定”，是否可能最终同时拥有 MDD 与大语言模型两边的缺点——既不灵活，又不确定。

EN

To be clear, I am not nostalgic for my old MDD experience or arguing that we should bring it back. But as we explore specification-driven development today, we should study earlier attempts to generate code from specs and learn from them.

中文

需要说明的是，我并不是怀念过去的 MDD 经历，也不是主张把它重新带回来。但当我们今天探索规格驱动开发时，应该回顾过去那些“从规格生成代码”的尝试，并从中吸取经验。

Conclusions结论

EN

In my own use of AI-assisted coding, I also often spend time carefully crafting some form of spec before giving it to a coding agent. The general principle of spec-first is therefore clearly valuable in many situations, and there is strong demand for guidance on how to structure such specs. Among the questions I currently hear most often from practitioners are: “How should I structure my memory bank?” and “How do I write a good specification and design document for AI?”

中文

在我自己使用 AI 辅助编程时，也经常会先花时间认真编写某种形式的规格说明，再交给编程智能体。因此，“规格优先”的总体原则在许多场景中无疑是有价值的，人们也非常需要关于如何组织这些规格说明的指导。目前从实践者那里最常听到的问题就包括：“记忆库应该如何组织？”以及“如何为 AI 编写一份好的规格说明和设计文档？”

EN

Yet the term “spec-driven development” is still poorly defined, and it has already undergone semantic diffusion. I have even heard people use “spec” as little more than a synonym for “detailed prompt”.

中文

然而，“规格驱动开发”这个术语目前仍缺乏清晰定义，而且已经出现语义扩散。我最近甚至听到有人把“spec”基本当成“详细提示词”的同义词。

EN

As for the tools I tried, I have listed many questions here about their real-world usefulness. I wonder whether some of them are feeding our existing workflows into AI agents too literally, thereby amplifying existing problems such as review overload and hallucination. The more elaborate approaches that generate large numbers of files make me think of the German compound word Verschlimmbesserung: in trying to make something better, are we actually making it worse?

中文

至于我尝试过的这些工具，本文已经列出了许多关于其现实价值的疑问。我怀疑其中一些工具是否过于机械地把现有工作流灌给 AI 智能体，结果反而放大了审查负担过重、幻觉等既有问题。尤其是那些会生成大量文件的复杂方案，总让我想到一个德语复合词 Verschlimmbesserung：我们是否在试图改进某件事的过程中，反而把它弄得更糟？
